summary:
Reconciled all three St. Brigid discharges under RBC-TOC-02. Each patient has a progress note, plus an update note for things that arrived while I was working (§8).

WALTER KIM (pt-0005)
- Furosemide changed from 20 mg daily to 40 mg twice daily (mr-t0001). The signed addendum (doc-00009) overrides the "40 mg daily" in the summary.
- Potassium chloride stopped (mr-00076), as the discharge summary says.
- Omeprazole kept. Pantoprazole was an inpatient formulary substitution, so it was not ordered.
- Metoprolol XL, atorvastatin and aspirin continue unchanged.
- Lisinopril (mr-00072): first kept on hold because potassium was 5.4 on 10/21. A repeat BMP on 10/23 (doc-00901) showed K 4.7 and SCr 1.21, which meets the discharge condition (SCr < 1.5), so I resumed it.
- An unsigned draft addendum (doc-00902) proposing furosemide 60 mg twice daily was not acted on, because only signed documents govern.
- FLAG: the system wouldn't let me close my earlier task on the potassium hold (task-t0003). It's no longer needed, so please close it.

TERENCE STARK (pt-0004)
- Carvedilol: first increased to 12.5 mg twice daily per the summary. A signed addendum arrived (doc-00904) saying the increase was reversed for HR 48-52 and lightheadedness, so it's back to 6.25 mg twice daily (mr-t0012).
- Aspirin and insulin 70/30 18 units twice daily continue unchanged.
- FLAG (comm-t0006): the discharge continues atorvastatin 80 mg (mr-00055), but the last fill was 03/04/2026, about 24% coverage of the 180 days before admission. Under §5b that counts as not taking it as prescribed, so I made no change.
- FLAG (comm-t0007): he's been filling glipizide 5 mg from Dr. Desai (Valley Endocrinology) at Lakeview Drug. We have no order for it and the discharge summary doesn't mention it. Nothing ordered or changed; please decide whether he continues it alongside insulin.

EARNEST ROBERTS (pt-0044)
- Insulin glargine 22 units, insulin lispro 6 units with meals and rosuvastatin 10 mg continue unchanged.
- Lisinopril 20 mg (mr-00373): I resumed it on the 10/22 outside BMP (SCr 1.08 meets the "SCr < 1.3" condition; K 4.6). A new potassium of 5.5 came in on 10/23 (obs-09002), so I put it back on hold under §7.
- FLAG: task-t0014 for you, due 10/27, to review the repeat potassium and decide whether to resume lisinopril.

The four inbox items that arrived during the work are completed and linked to the orders and notes. The other inbox items predate the work, aren't about these patients, and were left alone.

evidence.quote: The outside pharmacy claims history (doc-00007) shows glipizide 5 mg tablets, 30-day supply, filled 07/30, 08/29 and 09/28/2026 at Lakeview Drug, prescribed by Anil Desai, MD (Valley Endocrinology). There is no clinic order
Coverage of the 180 days before the 10/16 admission is about 44/180 days (24%), under the 80% threshold.
